title: Distributed circuit mesh with weighted fallback heuristics
creator: Ethan Kim
description: Goal: Implement a distributed 'circuit mesh' that applies circuit breakers at multiple granularities (dependency, model-version, tenant, route) and chooses safe, weighted fallback behaviors automatically. The mesh should: 1) compute trip decisions locally using a consistent set of signals (error rate, p99 latency, CPU/GPU queueing, recent successful fallback rate), 2) surface a global view for incident response and gradual policy rollouts, and 3) expose deterministic fallback selection with weighted heuristics (cached response, degraded model, remote region replica, rate-limited retries). This is intended to reduce outage blast radius, respect SLOs, and provide predictable degradation strategies for customer-facing routes.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Per-entity circuits: circuit state (closed, open, half-open) persists and is independently evaluable for dependency, model-version, tenant, and route.
2) Trip logic: implement windowed metrics + Bayesian smoothing for error-rate estimation; default threshold = 5% errors over 2m window with p99 latency threshold > 2s and minimum 100 requests.
3) Weighted fallback: fallback selection returns an ordered list with weights; default preference order: cached response (weight 100), degraded-local-model (weight 80), remote-region-replica (weight 60), low-cost-quantized-variant (weight 40), graceful error with fallback message (weight 10).
4) Safe half-open: half-open probes limited using token bucket per-circuit to avoid thundering herd.
5) Observability: dashboards show circuit states, trip reasons, fallback decisions, and request impact breakdowns. Alerts fire on correlated multi-circuit trips across regions.
6) Rollout + config: feature-flagged rollout with API and Console controls for thresholds, fallback ordering, and per-tenant overrides.
7) Runbook: documented playbook for human overrides and emergency open/close of meshes.
8) E2E tests and chaos experiments validate behavior under injected latency/failure patterns.

notes:
Implementation details: circuits run as lightweight stateful actors colocated with request router; state persisted in local redis with TTL + periodic snapshot to global store for global view.
Reasoning: local decision latency must be sub-ms; global store used only for dashboards and manual overrides.
Trip thresholds: default error_threshold = 0.05, min_requests = 100, lookback = 120s. Allow Console overrides and per-tenant tightening (eg enterprise tenants may set error_threshold=0.02).

Fallback weighting: weights are normalized into a softmax to pick a candidate; we also implement deterministic tie-breaker based on stable-hash of request id to ensure reproducible behavior for retries.
Trade-off: randomized fallback selection improves hit distribution but can complicate reproducibility for debugging. We default to deterministic selection for first try and randomized for subsequent retries.

Load-shedding policy: when global capacity deficit detected, mesh will consult tenant criticality and per-route importance score. Policy will shed lowest-priority requests first (background embedding batches, then low-priority chat messages), preferring graceful fallbacks over outright 503s.
We will expose a per-tenant 'priority' field that integrates with billing and SLA tiers.

Observability: emit 'circuit_event' with fields (circuit_id, level, reason, detected_at, resolution_est, fallback_chain) and 'fallback_decision' event with chosen_fallback, weights, cost_estimate, latency_est. These are indexed in our metrics pipeline for SRE queries.
Runbook highlights: operator can force-close/open circuits, pin fallback ordering, and escalate if >3 critical circuits open for >5 minutes. Emergency API documented in runbook link.
Next steps: finish UI for per-tenant controls (collab with DES-204), finalize chaos experiments (ENG-49000), and run a 10% traffic canary for 72 hours before full rollout.
